readings.title: Return of the Eastern Tribes
readings.subtitle: Faithful Service Rewarded
readings.text: [Joshua 22:1] Then Yehoshua called the Re’uḇĕnites, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Menashsheh, [2] and said to them, “You have guarded all that Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you, and have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you. [3] “You have not left your brothers these many days, up to this day, but have guarded the charge of the command of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [4] “And now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given rest to your brothers, as <dn>He</dn> spoke to them; so now turn back and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you beyond the Yardĕn. [5] “Only, take great heed to do the command and the Torah which Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you, to love <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to walk in all <dn>His</dn> ways, and to guard <dn>His</dn> commands, and to cleave to <dn>Him</dn>, and to serve <dn>Him</dn> with all your heart and with all your being.” [6] And Yehoshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents. [7] Now to half the tribe of Menashsheh Mosheh had given a possession in Bashan, but to the other half of it Yehoshua gave a possession among their brothers on this side of the Yardĕn westward. And indeed, when Yehoshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them too, [8] and spoke to them, saying, “Return with much riches to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, and with gold, and with bronze, and with iron, and with very many garments. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers.” [9] So the children of Re’uḇĕn, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Menashsheh returned, and departed from the children of Yisra’el at Shiloh, which is in the land of Kena‘an, to go to the country of Gil‘ad, to the land of their possession, which they possessed according to the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the hand of Mosheh.

readings.title: A Crisis of Unity
readings.subtitle: The Altar by the Jordan
readings.text: [Joshua 22:10] And they came to the regions of the Yardĕn which are in the land of Kena‘an, and the children of Re’uḇĕn, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Menashsheh built an altar there by the Yardĕn – a great altar to see. [11] And the children of Yisra’el heard it said, “See, the children of Re’uḇĕn, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Menashsheh have built an altar over against the land of Kena‘an, in the regions of the Yardĕn, on the side of the children of Yisra’el.” [12] And when the children of Yisra’el heard of it, the entire congregation of the children of Yisra’el gathered at Shiloh to go up to battle against them. [13] And the children of Yisra’el sent Pineḥas son of El‘azar the priest to the children of Re’uḇĕn, and to the children of Gad, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh, into the land of Gil‘ad, [14] and with him ten rulers, one ruler each from the chief house of every tribe of Yisra’el. And each one was the head of the house of his fathers among the thousands of Yisra’el. [15] And they came to the children of Re’uḇĕn, and to the children of Gad, and to half the tribe of Menashsheh, to the land of Gil‘ad, and they spoke with them, saying, [16] “Thus says all the congregation of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘What trespass is this that you have committed against the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, to turn back today from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, by building yourselves an altar, that you might rebel this day against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? [17] ‘Is the crookedness of Pe‘or too small for us, from which we are not cleansed to this day, although there was a plague in the congregation of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [18] that you must turn away this day from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? And it shall be, if you rebel today against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that tomorrow <dn>He</dn> is wroth with the entire congregation of Yisra’el. [19] ‘However, if the land of your possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, where the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stands, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [20] ‘Did not Aḵan son of Zeraḥ commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Yisra’el? And that man did not perish alone in his crookedness.’ ”

readings.title: A Witness Between Us
readings.subtitle: The Defense of the Eastern Tribes
readings.text: [Joshua 22:21] Then the children of Re’uḇĕn, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Menashsheh answered and said to the heads of the thousands of Yisra’el, [22] “<dn>El Elohim YeHoVaH</dn>! <dn>El Elohim YeHoVaH</dn>! <dn>He</dn> knows, and let Yisra’el know! If it is in rebellion, or if in trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not save us this day. [23] “If we have built ourselves an altar to turn from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, or if to offer on it burnt offerings or grain offerings, or if to offer peace offerings on it, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> require it. [24] “But in truth, we have done it for fear, for a reason, saying, ‘In time to come your sons might speak to our sons, saying, “What have you to do with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el? [25] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made the Yardĕn a border between you and us, you children of Re’uḇĕn and children of Gad. You have no portion in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” So your sons would make our sons cease fearing <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ [26] “Therefore we said, ‘Let us now prepare to build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering nor for slaughter, [27] but to be a witness between you and us and our generations after us, that we might perform the service of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before <dn>Him</dn> with our burnt offerings, and with our slaughterings, and with our peace offerings; that your sons might not say to our sons in time to come, “You have no portion in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” ’ [28] “Therefore we said that it shall be, when they say this to us or to our generations in time to come, that we shall say, ‘See the pattern of the altar of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which our fathers made, not for burnt offering nor for slaughter, but it is a witness between you and us.’ [29] “Far be it from us that we should rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and turn from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> this day, to build an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, or for slaughter, besides the altar of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> which is before <dn>His</dn> Dwelling Place.” [30] And when Pineḥas the priest and the rulers of the congregation, the heads of the thousands of Yisra’el who were with him, heard the words that the children of Re’uḇĕn and the children of Gad and the children of Menashsheh spoke, it was good in their eyes. [31] And Pineḥas son of El‘azar the priest said to the children of Re’uḇĕn, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Menashsheh, “This day we know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in our midst, because you have not committed this trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Now you have delivered the children of Yisra’el out of the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [32] And Pineḥas son of El‘azar the priest, and the rulers, returned from the children of Re’uḇĕn and from the children of Gad, from the land of Gil‘ad to the land of Kena‘an, to the children of Yisra’el, and brought back word to them. [33] And the matter was good in the eyes of the children of Yisra’el, and the children of Yisra’el blessed <dn>Elohim</dn>. And they spoke no more of going up against them to battle, to destroy the land where the children of Re’uḇĕn and Gad dwelt. [34] And the children of Re’uḇĕn and the children of Gad called the altar, ‘Witness,’ “For it is a witness between us that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>.”

readings.title: Joshua’s Farewell
readings.subtitle: A Warning Against Idolatry
readings.text: [Joshua 23:1] And it came to be, a long time after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had given rest to Yisra’el from all their enemies round about, that Yehoshua was old, advanced in years. [2] And Yehoshua called for all Yisra’el, for their elders, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers, and said to them, “I am old, advanced in years. [3] “And you have seen all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has done to all these nations because of you, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who was fighting for you. [4] “See, I have divided to you by lot these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from the Yardĕn, with all the nations that I have cut off, as far as the Great Sea westward. [5] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>He</dn> thrusts them out from before you and shall drive them out from before you, and you shall possess their land, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken to you. [6] “And you shall be very strong to guard and to do all that is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, so as not to turn aside from it right or left, [7] so as not to go in among these nations, these who remain among you. And do not make mention of the name of their mighty ones, nor swear by them, nor serve them nor bow down to them. [8] “But cleave to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as you have done to this day. [9] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has driven out from before you great and strong nations. But as for you, no one has stood against you to this day. [10] “One man of you chases a thousand, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who is fighting for you, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you. [11] “And you shall take great heed to yourselves to love <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [12] “But if you turn away at all and cleave to the remnant of these nations, these who remain among you, and intermarry with them, and go in to them and they to you, [13] know for certain that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is no longer going to drive out these nations from before you. But they shall be snares and traps to you, and a scourge on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you. [14] “And see, this day I am going the way of all the earth. And you know in all your hearts and in all your beings that not one word of all the good words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken concerning you has failed; all have come to pass for you, not one word of them has failed. [15] “And it shall be, that as all the good words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has spoken to you have come upon you, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings upon you every evil word, until <dn>He</dn> has destroyed you from this good land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you, [16] when you transgress the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> commanded you, and shall go and serve other mighty ones, and bow down to them. Then the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall burn against you, and you shall perish quickly from the good land which <dn>He</dn> has given you.”

readings.title: The Covenant at Sheḵem
readings.subtitle: Recounting the History of Israel
readings.text: [Joshua 24:1] And Yehoshua gathered all the tribes of Yisra’el to Sheḵem and called for the elders of Yisra’el, for their heads, for their judges, and for their officers. And they presented themselves before <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] And Yehoshua said to all the people, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, ‘<dq>Your fathers, including Teraḥ, the father of Aḇraham and the father of Naḥor, dwelt on the other side of the River in olden times, and they served other mighty ones.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> took your father Aḇraham from the other side of the River, and led him throughout all the land of Kena‘an, and increased his seed, and gave him Yitsḥaq.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And to Yitsḥaq <dn>I</dn> gave Ya‘aqoḇ and Ěsaw. And to Ěsaw <dn>I</dn> gave the mountains of Sĕ‘ir to possess, but Ya‘aqoḇ and his children went down to Mitsrayim.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> sent Mosheh and Aharon, and <dn>I</dn> plagued Mitsrayim, according to what <dn>I</dn> did in its midst. And afterward <dn>I</dn> brought you out.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> brought your fathers out of Mitsrayim, and you came to the sea. And the Mitsrites pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> put thick darkness between you and the Mitsrites, and brought the sea on them and covered them. And your eyes saw what <dn>I</dn> did in Mitsrayim. And you dwelt in the wilderness for a long time.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> brought you into the land of the Amorites, who dwelt beyond the Yardĕn, and they fought with you. And <dn>I</dn> gave them into your hand, and you possessed their land, and <dn>I</dn> destroyed them from before you.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And Balaq son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ, arose and fought against Yisra’el, and sent and called for Bil‘am son of Be‘or to curse you.</dq> [10] <dq>‘But <dn>I</dn> refused to listen to Bil‘am, so he continued to bless you, and <dn>I</dn> delivered you out of his hand.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And you passed over the Yardĕn and came to Yeriḥo. And the masters of Yeriḥo fought against you – the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Kena‘anites, and the Ḥittites, and the Girgashites, the Hiwites, and the Yeḇusites – and <dn>I</dn> gave them into your hand.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> sent the hornet before you which drove them out from before you, the two sovereigns of the Amorites, but not with your sword or with your bow.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> have given you a land for which you did not labour, and cities which you did not build, and you dwell in them. You eat of the vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant.’</dq>

readings.title: Choose You This Day
readings.subtitle: The Witness Stone
readings.text: [Joshua 24:14] “And now, fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, serve <dn>Him</dn> in perfection and in truth, and put away the mighty ones which your fathers served on the other side of the River and in Mitsrayim, and serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [15] “And if it seems evil in your eyes to serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, choose for yourselves this day whom you are going to serve, whether the mighty ones which your fathers served that were on the other side of the River, or the mighty ones of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [16] And the people answered and said, “Far be it from us to forsake <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to serve other mighty ones; [17] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage, who did those great signs before our eyes, and has preserved us in all the way that we went and among all the people through whose midst we passed. [18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drove out from before us all the people, even the Amorites who dwelt in the land. We too serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is our <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [19] And Yehoshua said to the people, “You are not able to serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is a set-apart <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>He</dn> is a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn>. <dn>He</dn> does not bear with your transgression and with your sins. [20] “If you forsake <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and serve foreign mighty ones, then <dn>He</dn> shall turn and do you evil and consume you, after <dn>He</dn> has done you good.” [21] And the people said to Yehoshua, “No, but we serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>!” [22] And Yehoshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for yourselves, to serve <dn>Him</dn>.” And they said, “We are witnesses!” [23] “And now, put away the foreign mighty ones which are in your midst, and incline your heart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el.” [24] And the people said to Yehoshua, “We serve <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, and we obey <dn>His</dn> voice.” [25] And Yehoshua made a covenant with the people that day, and laid on them a law and a right-ruling in Sheḵem. [26] And Yehoshua wrote these words in the Book of the Torah of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And he took a large stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] And Yehoshua said to all the people, “See, this stone is a witness to us, for it has heard all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke to us. And it shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [28] And Yehoshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.

readings.title: The End of an Era
readings.subtitle: Burials of Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar
readings.text: [Joshua 24:29] And it came to be after these matters that Yehoshua son of Nun, the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, died, one hundred and ten years old. [30] And they buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath Seraḥ, which is in the mountains of Ephrayim, on the north side of Mount Ga‘ash. [31] And Yisra’el served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of Yehoshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Yehoshua, who had known all the works of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had done for Yisra’el. [32] And the bones of Yoseph, which the children of Yisra’el had brought up out of Mitsrayim, they buried at Sheḵem, in the plot of ground which Ya‘aqoḇ had bought from the sons of Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem for one hundred pieces of silver, and which had become an inheritance of the children of Yoseph. [33] And El‘azar son of Aharon died. And they buried him in a hill that belonged to Pineḥas his son, which was given to him in the mountains of Ephrayim.
